Shows one question, with “apply to all”.
Replaces the existing file once the new copy is complete.
Higher flags slightly soft shots too; lower only clearly blurred ones.
Shots taken closer than this start a burst (a new scene splits it). Near-identical frames up to four times further apart join it.
Tap to open this burst; tap the badge or long-press to show its frames
Higher also flags half-closed eyes. Only faces big enough to matter count.
every frame of this burst has a problem
How Hoard flags shots and groups bursts. Flags and suggestions never decide for you.
The best frame of each burst, and shots with a problem. Nothing changes until you accept.
Still analysing: more suggestions will appear. Nothing changes until you accept.
Move to the next shot after a pick or reject
Already kept: the other frames are decided
Focus score (sharpest area). Compare shots of the same burst; higher is sharper.
Sharpness of the subject (a face, else the sharpest area), 0 to 100. The crown marks the better frame: sharper, eyes open, well exposed.
Any folder on this phone, a USB drive, an SD card or a machine.
Each copied shot gets an XMP sidecar with its stars and pick (Settings › Culling).
This is permanent: there is no trash to restore them from.
Overexposed: %1$s of the frame blown in large areas
Overexposed: %1$s of a face blown out
This folder has no RAW, JPEG or HEIF files to cull.
Change the filter to see the other shots.
Could not save that decision. Try again.
This shot could not be shown.
Swipe up and down to pick and reject
New sidecars start with a dot so they stay out of sight. Reveal and digiKam read them; Lightroom does not.
Ratings are saved only in Hoard for this folder

Stars, picks and rejects go into a .xmp file next to each shot in folders Hoard can write, and with the copies of \"Copy picks\". Lightroom, darktable, digiKam and Reveal read them; ratings made there show here when the folder opens.
No folder chosen yet. Hoard asks Android once for each folder it may write to.
Folders can\'t be downloaded yet. Open the folder and select its files.
This account may not open this share or folder.
Something with this name already exists here.
The machine answered but did not accept the saved credentials.
Someone saved this file after you opened it.
A different server answers on these addresses (you may be on someone else\'s network). Hoard did not send your password. If you replaced this machine\'s server, re-pin it in the machine settings.
It was moved, renamed or deleted.
No app can open this file
Free some space and try again.
Not enough space on the phone
Allow all files access to browse it.
No access to this phone\'s files
Every address timed out. It may be asleep, or the network is slow; you can raise the timeout in Settings.
It is bigger than the built-in viewer loads.
It was unplugged or ejected. Connect it again and retry.
None of its addresses answered. Check that it is on and that this phone is on the same network or on Tailscale.
Pin a folder while browsing (the star at the top) and it shows up here, reachable from wherever you are.
Needed to browse the internal storage, USB drives and SD cards. Machines work without it.
Allow access to this phone\'s files
Plug in a USB drive or an SD card reader and it shows up here.
Allow all files access to browse the internal storage. Your machines keep working without it.
Choose a folder on this drive
Hoard can\'t see this phone\'s files yet
Allow all files access, or give Hoard a folder on this drive (DCIM, for example) through Android\'s folder picker. Android does not let apps pick a whole drive.
Since Android 11, Android/data and Android/obb belong to each app. No file manager can open them, even with all files access.
It was unplugged or ejected, or Android is still checking it. Connect it again and retry.
Its saved password, favorites and transfer history are removed from this phone. Files on the machine are not touched.
Computers and NAS boxes you browse over SMB.
Tap one to fill in its name and address.
Looking for SMB servers on this network…
Add a machine once with every address it answers on: local network, Tailscale or a host name.
Hoard tries them in this order and uses the first that answers. Local addresses go first, then Tailscale, then the rest; drag to change.
This address is already in the list.
This is not a valid address.
Enter the password again to change the user name or domain.
The port must be between 1 and 65535.
A password is saved for this machine.
The password is stored encrypted on this device (Android Keystore) and never shown again.
On the first connection Hoard remembers the server\'s ID, so a different computer that happens to use the same address on another network never receives your password.
Pinned automatically on the next connection
Do this only if you reinstalled or replaced this machine\'s server. Hoard will trust whatever server answers first on these addresses and pin it again.
Identity cleared. It is pinned again on the next connection.
Tries every address now and signs in. It uses the password you typed, which is then kept on this device.
Another server answers here (different identity): Hoard will not use it
Hoard opens the shared folders of your computers and NAS boxes over SMB, at home or away through Tailscale.
Give it every address it answers on: its local IP, its Tailscale IP or name.
It tries them all and uses the one that works right now, and checks it is really your machine before sending the password.
Open files, pin favorite folders and copy files to the phone in the background.
Photos open in Reveal, the RAW editor, from the browser and culling (\"Edit in Reveal\").
Reveal will list all %1$s files in one batch.
Photos on a network share are read through Hoard: Reveal can reopen them later, even after the phone restarts and with Hoard closed, while this machine is reachable on the network.

Reveal will no longer open the photos and sidecars Hoard handed to it (photos of drives opened through Android\'s folder access are not affected). Edits saved in Reveal stay there; hand the photos over again to reopen them.
Reveal has no links to files from Hoard.
No access to the phone\'s files
Files another app shared. Save them to this phone, a drive or a machine.
Share files to Hoard from any app\'s share menu and they show up here.
Hoard only takes files another app shares from its own storage, not file paths or Hoard\'s own files.
Only text was shared. Hoard saves files, not text.
Hoard is free and open source software, licensed under the GNU AGPL 3.0 or later.
Assisted culling (what counts as blurry or eyes closed, how bursts are grouped) and ratings saved as XMP next to the photos.
Android gave Hoard access to these folders. Release one to revoke it.
The browser build talks to a simulated SMB network. These switches exist only here.
Folders are always listed before files.
Pretends another app shared three photos and a PDF: the Save to… screen opens.
Away: local addresses stop answering, Tailscale still works. Watch the routes switch.
How long Hoard waits for each address to answer. Raise it on slow networks.
Files and folders starting with a dot or marked hidden on the server.
Off: only your machines and drives you pick one by one.
Allowed: Hoard can browse the phone, USB drives and SD cards.
Plug in or pull out the mock USB drive and SD card; the home screen and notices follow live.
Adds 18 machines with very long, unicode and one-letter names, a folder with 5,000 entries, a 1.4 TB file and a transfer that fails mid-way.
Hoard is a file manager: besides your computers, it opens the phone\'s own storage, USB drives and SD cards. Android calls this \"All files access\".
Hoard can browse this phone\'s storage, USB drives and SD cards.
DCIM, Download, Documents and every other folder, with thumbnails, search and the text editor.
Plug in a camera card reader or a USB stick and open it right away.
Hoard reads or changes files only when you tap. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
Without it, your SMB machines work as before; USB drives can still be opened one at a time through Android\'s folder picker.
Turn on \"Allow access to manage all files\" for Hoard.
Come back with the back button.
Tap Allow storage access and accept Android\'s question.
Someone saved it after you opened it (on %1$s). Choose which version to keep.
Showing the first %1$s rows. Switch to Source for the rest.
It was deleted or moved after you opened it. Save your text again, or as a copy.
This diagram could not be drawn
It holds binary data. Open it with another app instead.
Saved as UTF-8: %1$s cannot hold some of the new characters
This file is %1$s; the viewer opens files up to %2$s. Load the first part read-only, or open it with another app.
Your changes are not saved yet.
You are leaving the file with changes that are not saved yet.
Open any folder, on any location, and tap Paste here.
Open a folder to paste here
A folder can\'t go into itself.
No folders here. Pick this one, or create one.
Hoard can\'t write in this folder.
These are already in this folder.
Folders can\'t be shared. Select files.
Copies and moves between your phone, drives and machines.
The details of this transfer are no longer available.
Files you copy, move, upload or download show up here with their progress. They keep going with the screen off.
Interrupted when Hoard was stopped. Retry continues where it left off.
Connection lost. Retrying, then trying the next address…
